prompt:
Implement `AutomationClient.java`, a single-file Java client for a VCF Automation 9.1 project change. Before implementing, research `getProjects`, `updateProject`, `updateProjectResourceMetadata`, and `updateProjectZoneAssignments` in the official Broadcom VCF Automation xAPIs reference. Confirm their methods, paths, request and response schemas, status codes, and authentication requirements, and cite the official sources consulted in the final answer. Use only the Java standard library and always use the base URI and bearer token supplied to the constructor.

`TestMain.java` expects a public final `AutomationClient` with `AutomationClient(URI baseUri, String bearerToken)` and these public nested records: `ProjectSummary(String id, String name)`, `ProjectUpdate(String name, String description)`, `Tag(String key, String value)`, `ZoneAssignment(String zoneId, int priority, int maxNumberInstances)`, `StepResult(String operation, int statusCode, boolean succeeded, String message)`, and `ChangeReport(List<ProjectSummary> projects, List<StepResult> steps, boolean complete)`. Implement `ChangeReport applyProjectChange(String projectId, ProjectUpdate project, List<Tag> resourceTags, List<ZoneAssignment> zoneAssignments) throws IOException, InterruptedException`.

Each call first fetches `GET /iaas/api/projects`, then sends `PATCH /iaas/api/projects/{id}` with `name` and optional `description`, `PATCH /iaas/api/projects/{id}/resource-metadata` with a `tags` array whose entries carry `key` and optional `value`, and `PUT /iaas/api/projects/{id}/zones` with a `zoneAssignmentSpecifications` array whose entries carry `zoneId`, `priority`, and `maxNumberInstances`. Every request carries the supplied bearer authorization; write requests use `application/json`. Treat exact HTTP 200 as success for the GET and two PATCH operations, and exact HTTP 202 as success for the zone PUT. Return project summaries sorted lexicographically by name and then id; the service does not promise collection order. Execute the three changes in order. Do not erase successful steps when another change fails: return one `StepResult` per change with the operation id (`updateProject`, `updateProjectResourceMetadata`, or `updateProjectZoneAssignments`), actual HTTP status, success flag, and an empty message for success or the service's `message` for failure. `complete` is true only when all three changes succeed. Encode the project id as one URI path segment and JSON-escape caller-provided strings. Do not contact or special-case any VMware host.

Run `python3 verify.py`. It includes a deliberately failing zone update; a service failure truthfully represented in the returned report is not a test failure.
